review_notes:
I read all three proofs in the file: `radial_commutator_norm_le`, `norm_le_two_mul_norm_of_near_id` and `two_center_constant_recovery`. Each proof writes the target as a difference, applies the triangle inequality (`norm_sub_le`) with `norm_mul_le` or `le_opNorm`, and closes with a short absorption step (`mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left/right` on hA, then `nlinarith`).

The only reasoning shared between proofs is that absorption step. In `radial_commutator_norm_le` (lines 36–37) and `norm_le_two_mul_norm_of_near_id` (lines 49–50) it has the form ‖x‖ ≤ a + ε‖x‖ with ε ≤ 1/2, giving ‖x‖ ≤ 2a. This is a two-line real-number calculation, and the rubric explicitly excludes short calculations. Pulling it into a helper would mostly re-package `nlinarith` and would not make the proofs clearer.

The triangle-inequality calc blocks differ in their algebraic identity (a `noncomm_ring` operator identity versus applying operators to vectors) and in the bounds they produce. Sharing them would only move routine unfolding into a helper.

`two_center_constant_recovery` already reuses the other two lemmas rather than repeating their arguments.

I searched `lean/OAI/Geometry/RCD` for related material. The dual covector argument in `lean/OAI/Geometry/RCD/Coordinates/CovectorConstantRecovery.lean` (`covector_norm_le_two_comp`, `covector_constant_recovery`) has the same shape. However, it works with `c.comp A` in the space of functionals rather than evaluating `A v`, so `norm_le_two_mul_norm_of_near_id` cannot be applied there directly. A common generalisation would need extra abstraction over left or right actions, and its only shared content would again be the short absorption calculation. The imported `MatrixNormConversion.lean` has no matching absorption arguments.

Remaining uncertainty: I did not search the whole repository for other uses of this vector-form lemma pattern outside `Geometry/RCD`.
